name: Pearl Haverty
languages: Stage French ('Madame Perle, from Paris') and a few words of Portuguese from the Fox Point docks
equipment: Pocket revolver (a pearl-handled .32 that a stage magician gave her in 1919, 'so you can make a man disappear'), 5 loaded, in her handbag

A carpet bag of stage properties: a planchette, a slate with a false flap, a speaking trumpet, a black velvet cloth, luminous paint, a small bell on a thread, two ounces of cheesecloth and a tambourine

A letter from Mrs. Verna Tibbetts of Carrow Island, engaging 'Madame Perle' to hold a seance to contact her late husband Clyde, with $25 enclosed and $50 to come, and two closely written pages describing Clyde, his voice, his sayings and what his spirit should say
A good black dress, a fringed shawl, a turban with a paste brooch, and a plain grey coat for travelling
A deck of cards, a ten-cent dream book, and a rosary that was her grandmother's, which she does not use for anything and will not leave behind
Smelling salts, a cigarette case and a lighter
features: Something to Hold On To (Faithful origin: once per long rest, when gaining Dread, gain 1 fewer; advantage on saves against being charmed or compelled by a creature; no miracle in it, only staying yourself). What she holds on to is her grandmother's rosary, which she does not pray with and will not leave behind

The Thin Place (Sensitive: she knows when a presence is within 60 ft, though not where; she feels cold spots and wrongness first, and in each room the GM tells her the strongest emotion soaked into it. Once per scene she can open herself to the place and the GM gives one true impression, a glimpse, a voice, a smell, about a presence, an event or what the thing wants; the cost is a point of Dread, with no save. It never controls anything)

Read the Room (Sensitive: advantage on Insight checks to tell what a person is feeling, and she knows without a check when someone she speaks with is frightened, grieving or hiding something, though not what)

Closer to the Edge (Sensitive, 2nd level: Dread from The Thin Place can't take her past Dread 5; at Dread 3 or higher it gives two impressions instead of one, and she can sense where a presence is to within 10 ft)
Gift: Listener (Sensitive, 3rd level: her impressions come as voices; once per scene she can hear the last words spoken in a place where someone died, as the GM chooses to give them)

The Séance Trade (Medium background: spiritualist circles, performers and grieving families welcome 'Madame Perle', and she can arrange a séance in any town with a day's notice; she spots another performer's tricks without a check, and the GM tells her when something in a room is not a trick. The background itself grants nothing supernatural)

personality.traits: I talk to everyone as if we were old friends in a dressing room. I am theatrical when I am frightened and very plain when I am telling the truth, and people who know me know which is which. I touch people's hands when I talk to them; it is a trick, and it is also just me.
personality.ideals: The bereaved deserve comfort, and comfort is worth paying for, and nobody has ever been harmed by hearing that their mother loved them. That is what I have always told myself, and I believed it right up until the night I heard a woman who was not there.
personality.bonds: My Nana Haverty in Providence, who raised me, told fortunes in tea leaves for the neighbours and said I had 'the sight' and must never use it for money. Professor Septimus Orr, who taught me the trade and was ruined by a newspaperman with a flash camera. The dead, if they are really there, which I have spent ten years making sure I did not have to find out.
personality.flaws: I am a fraud and I have come to Carrow to do a fraud, with a script in my bag. I know it is wrong and I have done it so long that I do not know how to stop. And I am more afraid of the real thing than of anything a living person could do to me.

appearance: A small, lively woman of twenty-eight with a heart-shaped face, a cloud of dark red hair under a velvet turban, very large dark eyes made larger with kohl, long clever hands with rings on every finger, and a low warm voice she can throw to the back of a theatre. On stage, black silk and a paste brooch; off it, a plain grey coat and a cloche hat and nobody looks at her twice.
backstory: Pearl Haverty grew up in a Fox Point tenement in Providence, raised by a grandmother who read tea leaves for the neighbours and who told her, very seriously, that she had the sight and must never use it for money. When she was fourteen and her grandmother was dying, Pearl heard her grandmother's voice in the next room saying something that only made sense the next morning, and she was so frightened that she decided it had not happened. At seventeen she went on the vaudeville stage as a mind reader's assistant, and at twenty-one she was taught the spiritualist trade by Professor Septimus Orr of Boston: the cabinet, the trumpet, the cold reading, the cheesecloth. When a reporter named Garrity exposed the Professor in 1919, she went out on her own as Madame Perle, holding seances in parlours across New England for widows of the war and the influenza, and doing, she tells herself, more good than harm. She has never once felt anything at a seance that she did not put there herself, and she has worked very hard to keep it that way. In September a Mrs. Verna Tibbetts wrote from Carrow Island to engage her, with a script: Clyde's spirit should say he drowned peacefully, that the bell called him, that he forgives everyone, and that he wants Verna to have the insurance and go away to her sister's. It reads like a woman who wants a story told, and Pearl is good at telling stories. (Hook: on the mail boat, when the bell rings under the water, Pearl hears a woman's voice, very clearly, say 'Come. Please come.' Nobody else hears it. She recognises the man in the chesterfield coat from a photograph in a newspaper.)
